title: Nvidia Commits $3 Billion to Meta's Share Sale as Chip and AI Ties Deepen
dek: Nvidia will buy into Meta's $95 billion funding plan while AMD adds $1 billion, linking two chip suppliers more closely to Meta's Muse AI agents and data centers.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial view of the Facebook campus in Menlo Park, California, Meta's headquarters

keyPoints: Nvidia said it will invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering; AMD said it will invest $1 billion.
Meta has said it plans to raise $95 billion, starting with $35 billion in underwritten public equity offerings and $60 billion through an at-the-market program.
Nvidia says Meta will expand its use of Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs, and the two companies will work on Muse inference and training performance.
Meta shares fell about 1% and Nvidia was flat on Tuesday, according to CNBC; AMD rose about 3%.
body:
Nvidia said on Tuesday it will put $3 billion into Meta Platforms' equity offering, a move that ties the chipmaker more closely to one of the largest buyers of AI computing capacity. The announcement follows Meta's plan, unveiled on Monday, to raise $95 billion to pay for its AI infrastructure. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/nvidia-invest-meta.html)

## What was announced

Meta said it would initially raise $35 billion through underwritten public equity offerings and then add $60 billion through an at-the-market program. Meta's Monday statement said Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were interested in buying up to $5 billion of shares. [CNBC Africa](https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/nvidia-to-invest-3-billion-in-meta-as-tech-giants-deepen-ai-partnership)

According to Investing.com, Meta later upsized its common stock offering to $25 billion from $22.5 billion, with a depository share offering that could bring the total to as much as $37.5 billion. Meta priced the common stock at $625 a share and the depository shares at $50 each. [Yahoo Finance, citing Investing.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-invest-3-bln-meta-064611851.html)

## The product and hardware side

Nvidia's own release, dated October 26, says the companies will expand their work on Muse, Meta's family of AI models and agents, to improve inference and training performance. Meta also plans to expand its deployment of Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Vera CPU systems, along with Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4. [NVIDIA Newsroom](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-meta-to-expand-collaboration-on-muse-and-muse-family-of-models-amid-robust-growth)

Nvidia's release says the two companies will also consider work on its OpenShell reference architecture for deploying agents safely and its Sentry product for monitoring agent behavior. Those items are described as possibilities, not finished agreements.

AMD said its Helios racks are running at Meta and its EPYC processors power Muse, and that the two companies are building gigawatt-scale infrastructure. CNBC reported that AMD's $1 billion commitment is part of the same financing round. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/nvidia-invest-meta.html)

## Why it matters for the market

The immediate read is about supply and financing. Mizuho analyst Lloyd Walmsley told Investing.com the Meta equity raise helps remove part of an equity overhang, because investors had expected to wait until Class C shares were created in January 2027. Analysts quoted by Investing.com framed the pull-forward as a relief for the stock.

The risk is that Meta is raising equity while spending heavily on hardware. Its shareholders now carry more dilution, and its chip partners are investing in its funding round as well as selling it products. CNBC noted that Nvidia has been building stakes across the AI supply chain, including in OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel and xAI.

For Nvidia, the deal reinforces demand for its Vera Rubin platform and its networking products. For AMD, the $1 billion commitment and the reference to Helios racks in production put it in a similar position. Broadcom is named in Meta's announcement as an interested buyer but has not confirmed a purchase in the sources reviewed here.

## What to watch

The stock reaction on Tuesday was muted: CNBC reported Nvidia flat, AMD up about 3% and Meta down about 1%. The next test is how Meta prices and places the remaining at-the-market program, and whether Muse adoption continues to support the capital plan. Nothing in the sources reviewed sets a specific date for further offerings beyond the at-the-market program.

marketImpact.summary: The deal is a financing and demand signal. It removes some uncertainty about Meta's equity supply, supports Nvidia's and AMD's infrastructure outlook, and raises dilution and capex questions for Meta.
